Every checktor check exists for a reason, and that reason has a source. This page
maps each check to where its authority comes from -- with a link to the exact
section wherever one exists -- and to the severity tier that authority earns. For
the full argument behind any single check, read its help page (for example
`?diagnose_option_changes`), which spells out the reasoning and the exemptions. This
page is the map across all of them.

## The tiers, and what each one rests on

A check's severity tier tells you what kind of authority stands behind it.

- **`policy`** is a rule CRAN enforces, so breaking one can get a package rejected
  and a policy finding counts against a clean bill of health. Most are written in the
  [CRAN Repository Policy][policy] or [Writing R Extensions][wre], the two documents
  CRAN treats as binding, and some mirror a **CRAN incoming check**, one of the NOTEs
  that [`R CMD check --as-cran`][wre-check] raises against a submission. A handful are
  long-standing requirements reviewers apply that no clause in either manual actually
  states, and for those the [CRAN Cookbook][cookbook] is the written record. Restoring
  `options()`, `par()` and the working directory is the clearest example: it is one of
  the most common reasons a package is sent back, and neither manual mentions it.
- **`robustness`** is a real defect that CRAN will nonetheless let you ship, such as
  a `detectCores()` that can return `NA`. It counts toward the verdict too, because it
  can still crash a user.
- **`opinion`** is a convention that experienced maintainers and reviewers tend to
  ask for, with nothing enforcing it. Worth knowing, but it stays outside the default
  verdict, which is `policy` and `robustness` only.

The source column names which kind each check is. Many conventions are written down
in the [CRAN Cookbook][cookbook], the R Contributor guide to the problems that get
packages sent back, and the column links to the individual recipe wherever there is
one. Where a check has no citable source at all, it says so plainly.

## Code checks

| Check | Tier | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `seed_setting` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: a package "should not modify the global environment", and `set.seed()` writes `.Random.seed` there. Recipe: [Setting a Specific Seed][cb-seed]. |
| `print_cat_usage` | `policy` | [Cookbook: Using print()/cat()][cb-printcat]: diagnostic output belongs in `message()` or `warning()`, which a user can suppress. A reviewer requirement rather than a clause in the manuals. |
| `option_changes` | `policy` | [Cookbook: Change of Options, Graphical Parameters and Working Directory][cb-options]: restore anything a function changes, via `on.exit()`. Neither manual states this, but it is among the most common reasons a package is sent back. |
| `warn_option` | `policy` | [Cookbook: Setting options(warn = -1)][cb-warn]: the same requirement, for the warning level. |
| `home_writing` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: "Packages should not write in the user's home filespace ... nor anywhere else on the file system apart from the R session's temporary directory". Recipe: [Writing Files and Directories to the Home Filespace][cb-home]. |
| `globalenv_mod` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: "Packages should not modify the global environment (user's workspace)." Recipe: [Writing to the .GlobalEnv][cb-globalenv]. |
| `installed_packages` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: a package must not install other packages when it runs. Recipe: [Calling installed.packages()][cb-installed]. |
| `software_install` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: a package must not download and install external software at load or run time. Recipe: [Installing Software][cb-software]. |
| `core_usage` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: "If running a package uses multiple threads/cores it must never use more than two simultaneously". Recipe: [Using more than 2 Cores][cb-cores]. |
| `sys_setenv` | `policy` | No clause names environment variables, but they are session state exactly as `options()` are, and the same restore-on-exit requirement applies. See [Cookbook: Change of Options, Graphical Parameters and Working Directory][cb-options]. |
| `tf_usage` | `robustness` | No binding rule, but a documented one: [Cookbook: T/F Instead of TRUE/FALSE][cb-tf]. `T` and `F` are ordinary variables (see `?logical`) that can be rebound, so they are unsafe stand-ins. |
| `library_in_pkg` | `robustness` | [WRE: Package Dependencies][wre-deps]: package code should reach dependencies through `Imports` and `::`, not attach them with `library()`. |
| `detect_cores_robustness` | `robustness` | No formal rule. `?detectCores` states it returns "`NA` if the answer is unknown", and the arithmetic that usually follows then crashes. |
| `hardcoded_credentials` | `robustness` | No formal rule. A token or key committed to a package is public the moment it reaches CRAN and must be revoked. |
| `temp_cleanup` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Leaving Files in the Temporary Directory][cb-temp]. `tempdir()` is removed at session end, so an un-`unlink()`ed tempfile breaks no rule, which is why this stays advisory. |

## DESCRIPTION checks

| Check | Tier | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `software_names` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: "Refer to other packages and external software in single quotes". Recipe: [Formatting Software Names][cb-names]. |
| `language_names` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: the same rule, for programming-language and markup names. Recipe: [Formatting Software Names][cb-names]. |
| `description_quoted_quotes` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: double quotes are for book titles and similar; software names take single quotes. Recipe: [Formatting Software Names][cb-names]. |
| `license` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: an invalid or unrecognised `License` field is a rejection. Recipe: [LICENSE files][cb-license]. |
| `authors` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: a placeholder or malformed `Authors@R`, including a missing maintainer, is a rejection. Recipe: [Using Authors@R][cb-authors]. |
| `title_case` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: the `Title` "should use title case"; the [`--as-cran`][wre-check] incoming check flags one that does not. Recipe: [Title Case][cb-titlecase]. |
| `date_format` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: "the 'yyyy-mm-dd' format of the ISO 8601 standard is strongly recommended"; the [incoming check][wre-check] also flags a stale or future date. |
| `version_format` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: a `Version` is "a sequence of at least two ... non-negative integers"; the [incoming check][wre-check] flags a leading zero or an implausible value. |
| `encoding_utf8` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: a non-ASCII DESCRIPTION "should contain an 'Encoding' field"; the [incoming check][wre-check] flags a non-portable one. |
| `description_starts_with` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: "It is good practice not to start with the package name, 'This package' or similar"; flagged by the [incoming check][wre-check]. |
| `references` | `policy` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check]: it NOTEs a reference not written in the `<doi:...>` or `<arXiv:...>` form. Recipe: [References][cb-refs]. |
| `identifier_format` | `policy` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check]: it NOTEs a malformed ORCID or ROR identifier in `Authors@R`. |
| `license_year` | `robustness` | No binding rule. An unfilled `LICENSE` template, with `<YEAR>` or `<COPYRIGHT HOLDER>` left in, ships a placeholder. Recipe: [LICENSE files][cb-license]. |
| `spelling` | `opinion` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check] (aspell), but it needs a spell-check backend and is noisy, so checktor keeps it advisory. |
| `acronyms` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Explaining Acronyms][cb-acronyms]. Reviewers ask for an acronym to be spelled out once, but nothing enforces it. |
| `cph_role` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Using Authors@R][cb-authors] covers the roles, and a copyright-holder (`cph`) is commonly expected, though not required. |
| `description_length` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Description Length][cb-desclen]. A one-line `Description` is thin, and reviewers ask for more. |
| `title_length` | `opinion` | Convention only. A `Title` under about 65 characters is a common preference. |
| `title_redundant_phrases` | `opinion` | Convention only. Phrases like "R package to" are redundant in a `Title`. |
| `title_starts_with_article` | `opinion` | No rule. A mis-transplant of a real CRAN rule, kept callable but off by default. |
| `description_function_quotes` | `opinion` | No rule. An invented rule, kept callable but off by default. |

## Documentation checks

| Check | Tier | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `suggested_in_examples` | `policy` | [WRE: Suggested packages][wre-sugg]: a package from `Suggests` used in an example must be guarded so the example still runs without it. |
| `roxygen_usage` | `robustness` | No binding rule. A function tagged `@export` that never reached `NAMESPACE` is not actually exported. Recipe: [Repeated Rejections of Issues in Manuals If Using roxygen2][cb-roxygen]. |
| `unexported_example_ns` | `robustness` | No formal rule. An example that reaches for an unexported object will error when it runs. |
| `value_tags` | `opinion` | [WRE: Documenting functions][wre-doc] describes `\value{}` and [Cookbook: Missing \value-tags in .Rd-files][cb-value] is the recipe reviewers cite, but `R CMD check` does not require it. |
| `example_structure` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Structuring of Examples][cb-examples]. `\dontrun{}` should wrap only code that genuinely cannot run inside a check. |
| `donttest_vs_dontrun` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Structuring of Examples][cb-examples]: `\donttest{}` is the wrapper for examples that merely run long, where `\dontrun{}` is often reached for instead. |
| `missing_examples` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Structuring of Examples][cb-examples]. Exported functions are expected to carry an `\examples{}` block. |
| `commented_examples` | `opinion` | Convention only. An `\examples{}` block that is entirely commented out demonstrates nothing. |

## General checks

| Check | Tier | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `package_size` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: CRAN limits the size of the built tarball. Recipe: [Package Size][cb-size], which gives the practical figures. |
| `url_liveness` | `robustness` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check]: `--as-cran` fetches URLs and NOTEs 404s and redirects. It is opt-in here because it needs a network. |
| `readme_links` | `robustness` | No formal rule. A relative README link whose target is excluded from the tarball breaks on the package page. |
| `urls` | `opinion` | Convention only. Preferring `https://` is good advice, but CRAN's NOTE is about broken URLs rather than the scheme. |
| `news_file` | `opinion` | Convention only. A `NEWS` file is expected but not required. |

## CRAN policy checks

| Check | Tier | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `browser_calls` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: checks run non-interactively, so a debugging leftover such as `browser()` must not ship. |
| `file_operations` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: "Packages should not write ... anywhere ... apart from the R session's temporary directory". Recipe: [Writing Files and Directories to the Home Filespace][cb-home]. |
| `network_operations` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: "Packages which use Internet resources should fail gracefully with an informative message if the resource is not available". |
| `system_calls` | `robustness` | No flat rule. A raw `system()` or `system2()` call needs review for portability rather than being an automatic violation. |

## When checktor and an authority disagree

A tier is where a check's authority sits, not how strongly checktor feels about it.
A few checks are deliberately `opinion` because no authority backs them in either
direction, and two of those (`title_starts_with_article` and
`description_function_quotes`) are kept callable but left out of the default run for
the same reason. If a finding does not match your reading of the policy, the tier is
the first thing to look at: an `opinion` finding is a conversation, not a
requirement, and you can turn any check off through `Config/checktor` in your own
DESCRIPTION.
